subject: Microbiology
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A man with HIV (CD4 count 40/µL) has headache and fever. This CSF preparation is shown. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.A: A negative India-ink preparation does not exclude the diagnosis; cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) is substantially more sensitive
options.B: A mucicarmine stain of CSF is the recommended rapid bedside test
options.C: India ink is >99% sensitive in HIV and is the diagnostic test of choice
options.D: The organisms shown are Candida; start a mucosal-candidiasis dose of fluconazole only

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: The incidence of stroke is 20 per 1000 among hypertensives and 5 per 1000 among normotensives. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.A: The attributable risk percent is 4
options.B: Attributable risk percent is 75%, so three-quarters of the strokes among hypertensives are attributable to hypertension
options.C: The attributable risk (absolute) is 15%
options.D: The relative risk is 75%

subject: Pathology
stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of reversible cell injury?

options.A: Nuclear pyknosis, karyorrhexis and karyolysis
options.B: Myelin figures formed from degenerate phospholipids
options.C: Plasma-membrane blebbing and loss of microvilli
options.D: Cellular (hydropic) swelling, the earliest light-microscopic change

subject: Psychiatry
stem: A 28-year-old with bipolar disorder has had four distinct manic or depressive episodes in the last 11 months. TSH is normal. The mood stabiliser of choice is:

options.A: Venlafaxine
options.B: Amitriptyline
options.C: Lithium carbonate
options.D: Sodium valproate

subject: Pediatrics
concept: WHO Plan C – severe dehydration rate by age
stem: A 2-year-old has severe dehydration from acute diarrhoea and IV access is obtained. As per WHO Plan C, Ringer lactate should be given as:

options.A: 75 mL/kg of ORS over 4 hours
options.B: 20 mL/kg boluses over 15 minutes only, without completing 100 mL/kg
options.C: 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg in the next 2½ hours
options.D: 30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in the next 5 hours

subject: Medicine
stem: On day 3 of severe pneumonia, thyroid tests show low T3, high reverse T3 and a normal TSH. A week later, as the patient recovers, TSH is mildly raised and T4 is low-normal. The MOST likely explanation is:

options.A: A TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma
options.B: New primary hypothyroidism that must be treated immediately with thyroxine
options.C: Factitious thyrotoxicosis
options.D: Recovery from sick euthyroid syndrome (a transient TSH rise is expected; do not label this as primary hypothyroidism yet)

subject: Psychiatry
stem: A woman with bipolar disorder has had six mood episodes this year while taking lithium plus a recently added SNRI. TSH is normal. Besides reviewing adherence and substances, the MOST appropriate medication change is:

options.A: Stop lithium and start imipramine monotherapy
options.B: Increase the lithium dose and add a second antidepressant
options.C: Taper and stop the antidepressant, and switch the mood stabiliser to valproate (or add an anticonvulsant mood stabiliser)
options.D: Continue both drugs unchanged and start empirical thyroxine even though TSH is normal

subject: Orthopedics
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A child fell on an outstretched hand. The elbow and forearm X-rays are shown. The nerve MOST likely to be injured, and the expected deficit, is:

options.A: Anterior interosseous nerve — inability to make the 'OK' sign, with no sensory loss
options.B: Superficial radial nerve — sensory loss over the first web space only, with normal finger extension
options.C: Posterior interosseous nerve — finger and thumb drop without wrist drop and without sensory loss
options.D: Ulnar nerve — clawing of the ring and little fingers with palmar sensory loss

subject: Medicine
concept: WPW – pre-excited AF, drugs to avoid
stem: A young adult with known WPW presents with an irregular, very rapid, wide-complex tachycardia and a blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg with confusion. The MOST appropriate immediate treatment is:

options.A: An intravenous digoxin loading dose
options.B: Intravenous verapamil to slow the ventricular rate
options.C: Intravenous adenosine
options.D: Immediate synchronised DC cardioversion

subject: Surgery
stem: A 52-year-old is recovering from SEVERE acute gallstone pancreatitis. CT shows large peripancreatic fluid collections. He is now afebrile and tolerating oral intake. The recommended timing of cholecystectomy is:

options.A: Delayed until the collections have substantially resolved, typically after about 6 weeks
options.B: Only if a second attack of pancreatitis occurs
options.C: During the same admission, as soon as abdominal pain has settled
options.D: Emergency cholecystectomy within 24 hours of the original admission

subject: Pediatrics
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A 10-month-old with this chest X-ray becomes deeply cyanosed and limp after a long cry; the systolic murmur is much softer than usual. Which drug is CONTRAINDICATED in this situation?

options.A: Morphine
options.B: Intravenous dobutamine
options.C: Propranolol
options.D: Phenylephrine

subject: Surgery
stem: A patient is admitted with mild gallstone pancreatitis plus ascending cholangitis (fever, jaundice and hypotension that responds to fluids). After resuscitation, the MOST appropriate biliary plan is:

options.A: Interval cholecystectomy after 6–8 weeks, and no ERCP
options.B: Emergency cholecystectomy within 24 hours, without ERCP
options.C: Urgent ERCP with sphincterotomy, then laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the same admission once the pancreatitis has settled
options.D: Conservative treatment only; both ERCP and surgery are deferred unless a second attack occurs

subject: Orthopedics
concept: Epiphyseal bone tumours – age of physis
stem: A 13-year-old has an epiphyseal lytic lesion of the proximal humerus with stippled chondroid calcification; the growth plate is still open. The MOST likely diagnosis is:

options.A: Chondroblastoma
options.B: Giant cell tumour (osteoclastoma)
options.C: Conventional osteosarcoma
options.D: Ewing sarcoma

subject: Microbiology
stem: Cryptococcal meningitis is confirmed in a patient with advanced HIV. The preferred INDUCTION therapy is:

options.A: High-dose acyclovir plus corticosteroids as first-line induction
options.B: Amphotericin B plus flucytosine, followed by fluconazole consolidation
options.C: Fluconazole monotherapy from day 1 at a standard mucosal-candidiasis dose
options.D: Albendazole plus praziquantel

subject: Pediatrics
concept: WHO Plan C – severe dehydration rate by age
stem: A 10-month-old with severe dehydration is started on WHO Plan C. After the first 30 mL/kg of Ringer lactate has been given, the remaining 70 mL/kg should be infused over:

options.A: 2½ hours
options.B: 4 hours as oral ORS (Plan B)
options.C: 15 minutes, as a further shock bolus
options.D: 5 hours

subject: OBG
stem: Which statement about the Government of India (DIPSI) guideline for GDM is CORRECT?

options.A: 75 g oral glucose is given irrespective of the last meal, and a 2-hour venous plasma glucose ≥140 mg/dL diagnoses GDM
options.B: Screening is done only once, at 24–28 weeks, and never at the first antenatal visit
options.C: A 50 g glucose-challenge 1-hour value ≥140 mg/dL is itself diagnostic of GDM
options.D: The diagnostic 2-hour cut-off is ≥200 mg/dL, as used for overt diabetes in non-pregnant adults

subject: Medicine
stem: A septic ICU patient with no prior thyroid disease has low T3, low-normal T4, normal TSH and a raised reverse T3. The MOST appropriate action is:

options.A: Diagnose primary hypothyroidism and give a high loading dose of thyroxine
options.B: Start levothyroxine now, because low T3 and T4 confirm hypothyroidism
options.C: Do not start thyroid hormone; treat the underlying illness (this is sick euthyroid / non-thyroidal illness)
options.D: Start liothyronine (T3) replacement, because T3 is the active hormone

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: Which of the following multi-dose vaccines MAY be used in subsequent sessions for up to 28 days if all open-vial conditions are met?

options.A: Measles–rubella (MR) vaccine
options.B: Japanese encephalitis (JE) vaccine
options.C: Pentavalent (DPT–HepB–Hib) vaccine
options.D: BCG vaccine

subject: Pediatrics
concept: Measles – infectivity, Koplik spots, vitamin A
stem: A 14-month-old with clinically confirmed measles has no eye signs of vitamin A deficiency. As per WHO, vitamin A should be given as:

options.A: No vitamin A, unless xerophthalmia is already present
options.B: 200,000 IU orally today, repeated the next day
options.C: 50,000 IU daily for 2 weeks
options.D: 100,000 IU once only, because the child is under 2 years

subject: Medicine
stem: HIT has been confirmed. Heparin was stopped and argatroban started. The platelet count has now risen to 160 × 10⁹/L. The appropriate plan for warfarin is:

options.A: Give a 5 mg warfarin loading dose plus a platelet transfusion, then stop argatroban immediately
options.B: Warfarin should have been started on the day HIT was diagnosed, as soon as heparin was stopped, regardless of the platelet count
options.C: Warfarin must never be used at any time after an episode of HIT
options.D: Warfarin may be started now, overlapped with argatroban until a stable therapeutic INR is reached (accounting for argatroban's effect on the INR)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A 13-year-old obese boy has had knee pain and a limp for 6 weeks. The frog-lateral hip radiograph is shown; a line has been drawn along the superior femoral neck. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.A: The line missing the epiphysis means the hip is normal, so no treatment is required
options.B: This is Klein's (Trethowan's) line; it misses or cuts less of the epiphysis than normal, and treatment is in-situ screw fixation without forceful reduction
options.C: This appearance in a 13-year-old is typical of Perthes disease and is treated by observation only
options.D: Forced closed reduction under anaesthesia is the treatment of choice to restore anatomy

subject: Psychiatry
stem: A patient who has been stable on lithium for years develops coarse tremor, vomiting and ataxia shortly after an over-the-counter analgesic is started for backache. The drug MOST likely to have raised the lithium level is:

options.A: Theophylline
options.B: Ibuprofen
options.C: Acetazolamide
options.D: Mannitol

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: Under India's national vitamin A prophylaxis programme, the FIRST dose, given at 9 months of age with MR-1, is:

options.A: 2 lakh IU, because every prophylactic dose is 2 lakh IU
options.B: 2 lakh IU daily for 3 days
options.D: 50,000 IU as a single dose

subject: Microbiology
stem: A jaundiced adult has the following serology: HBsAg negative, anti-HBs negative, total anti-HBc positive and IgM anti-HBc positive. The BEST interpretation is:

options.A: Resolved past infection with lasting immunity
options.B: Inactive chronic HBsAg carrier
options.C: Successful hepatitis B vaccination
options.D: Window period of acute hepatitis B (IgM anti-HBc is the only marker of ongoing acute infection)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A 7-month-old known to have tetralogy of Fallot becomes irritable, deeply cyanosed and hyperpnoeic. After calling for help, the FIRST immediate manoeuvre is:

options.A: Start dobutamine and defer oxygen until an arterial blood gas is available
options.B: Place the infant in the knee-chest position and give oxygen
options.C: Start an isoprenaline infusion to raise cardiac output
options.D: Give intravenous digoxin as the first drug

subject: Medicine
stem: On day 8 of unfractionated heparin, platelets fall from 280 to 90 × 10⁹/L and a new pulmonary embolus is diagnosed. HIT is confirmed. Which of the following is CONTRAINDICATED at this moment?

options.A: Starting warfarin today as the sole anticoagulant, while the platelet count is still 90 × 10⁹/L
options.B: Stopping all heparin, including heparin flushes
options.C: Starting intravenous argatroban
options.D: Starting fondaparinux once the patient is stable

subject: Pediatrics
concept: Measles – infectivity, Koplik spots, vitamin A
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A 2-year-old had fever, cough and red watery eyes for 3 days. This rash then began behind the ears and spread downward over the trunk. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.A: The child may return to daycare as soon as the fever settles, even if the rash is only 1 day old
options.B: Vitamin A is withheld unless Bitot spots or xerophthalmia are already present
options.C: The commonest cause of death from this illness is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE)
options.D: Vitamin A is given to this child even if there are no eye signs — two age-appropriate doses 24 hours apart

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Which statement about Monteggia and Galeazzi fracture-dislocations is CORRECT?

options.A: Monteggia is a fracture of the distal radius with DRUJ dislocation; the nerve at risk is the ulnar nerve
options.B: Galeazzi is a fracture of the ulna with radial-head dislocation; the nerve at risk is the anterior interosseous nerve
options.C: Monteggia is a fracture of the ulna with dislocation of the radial head; the nerve at risk is the posterior interosseous nerve
options.D: Both injuries typically present with a median-nerve palsy at the carpal tunnel

subject: Physiology
stem: Which of the following hormones acts through a receptor that signals via the JAK–STAT pathway?

options.A: Glucagon
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Erythropoietin

subject: Medicine
concept: WPW – pre-excited AF, drugs to avoid
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A 22-year-old with palpitations has this resting ECG. He later presents with an irregular, wide-complex tachycardia at 230/min but is haemodynamically stable. Which drug is CONTRAINDICATED?

options.A: Intravenous ibutilide
options.B: Synchronised DC cardioversion
options.C: Intravenous procainamide
options.D: Intravenous digoxin

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: A child starts vitamin A prophylaxis on time at 9 months (1 lakh IU) and then receives 2 lakh IU every 6 months from 16–18 months until 5 years of age, inclusive. The complete schedule is:

options.A: 10 doses totalling 20 lakh IU
options.B: 5 doses totalling 10 lakh IU
options.C: 8 doses totalling 16 lakh IU
options.D: 9 doses totalling 17 lakh IU

subject: Psychiatry
stem: A patient stable on lithium needs an additional drug. Which of the following is LEAST likely to raise the serum lithium concentration?

options.A: Hydrochlorothiazide
options.B: Theophylline
options.C: Enalapril
options.D: Ibuprofen

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: Under India's open vial policy, which opened vaccine must be discarded at the end of the immunisation session (or within 4 hours of reconstitution) and cannot be kept for 28 days?

options.A: Measles–rubella (MR) vaccine
options.B: Hepatitis B vaccine
options.C: Pentavalent (DPT–HepB–Hib) vaccine
options.D: Oral polio vaccine (OPV)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 14-year-old obese boy has isolated left knee pain; the knee examination and knee X-ray are normal. On flexing the ipsilateral hip, the thigh rolls into obligatory external rotation (Drehmann sign). The MOST appropriate next step is:

options.A: Obtain urgent hip radiographs (AP and frog-lateral) and plan in-situ fixation if SCFE is confirmed; do not forcefully reduce
options.B: Start high-dose steroids for presumed transient synovitis and review in 6 weeks
options.C: Manipulate the hip into internal rotation under sedation to 'relocate' the epiphysis
options.D: Reassure and discharge, because a normal knee X-ray excludes hip pathology

subject: Medicine
stem: A 19-year-old has recurrent cramps, BP 110/70 mmHg, K⁺ 2.6 mEq/L, metabolic alkalosis, urine chloride 50 mEq/L, low serum magnesium and low urinary calcium. He is not on diuretics. The MOST likely diagnosis is:

options.A: Gitelman syndrome
options.B: Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome)
options.C: Bartter syndrome
options.D: Repeated self-induced vomiting

subject: Orthopedics
concept: Epiphyseal bone tumours – age of physis
stem: IMAGE-BASED: A 32-year-old has knee pain. The radiograph shows an eccentric lytic lesion in the distal femoral epiphysis reaching the subchondral bone. The physis is fused. The MOST likely diagnosis is:

options.A: Chondroblastoma
options.B: Giant cell tumour (osteoclastoma)
options.C: Conventional osteosarcoma
options.D: Ewing sarcoma

subject: Medicine
stem: A patient with prolonged vomiting has metabolic alkalosis, K⁺ 3.0 mEq/L and a urine chloride of 8 mEq/L. This alkalosis is BEST described as:

options.A: Chloride-resistant alkalosis due to Conn syndrome
options.B: Chloride-resistant alkalosis due to Bartter syndrome
options.C: Chloride-responsive (saline-responsive); the low urine chloride reflects extra-renal chloride loss
options.D: A primary respiratory alkalosis from anxiety, not a metabolic disorder

subject: OBG
stem: A 26-year-old at 24 weeks is given 75 g oral glucose in the antenatal clinic 1 hour after breakfast (she was not asked to fast). The 2-hour venous plasma glucose is 152 mg/dL. As per the Government of India DIPSI guideline, this is:

options.A: Overt (frank) diabetes mellitus, because the value is above 140 mg/dL
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus (non-fasting 75 g test; 2-hour value ≥140 mg/dL)
options.C: An incomplete test; a 100 g 3-hour OGTT is required before any diagnosis can be made
options.D: A normal result, because the test is invalid unless it is performed fasting

subject: Microbiology
stem: A healthcare worker's hepatitis B serology is: HBsAg negative, anti-HBs 180 mIU/mL, anti-HBc negative. This pattern indicates:

options.A: Immunity due to hepatitis B vaccination
options.B: Past infection with recovery
options.C: The window period of acute hepatitis B
options.D: Chronic hepatitis B with an HBsAg escape mutant

subject: PSM / Community Medicine
stem: In a cohort study, the incidence of coronary events is 36 per 1000 among smokers and 12 per 1000 among non-smokers. The attributable risk percent (AR%) is:
